A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WebDS. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial revisions to presentation and reported evaluation settings.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebDS agent evaluations in Tables 4–5, human validation of the evaluator, repeated-scoring results, and qualitative failure analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original agent evaluations and adds GPT-5.1 results, a human task-completion study, expanded evaluator validation, and quantified failure analysis.

M1.justification: The task-processing pipeline and full-trajectory binary/1–5 evaluation procedure remain unchanged. v2's expanded BrowserUse appendix retains the AXTree indexing, action-prompt modifications, and CSV tools described in v1. Additional control-loop, memory, and caching details do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 describes evaluation using all 29 websites in Docker; v2 explicitly reports Table 5 on WebDS-live and limits Dockerized coverage to a subset. This materially revises the reported evaluation environments, while retaining the 870-task suite and website/domain coverage. The PDFs do not establish that the retained results were rerun.

E2.justification: v2 retains the nine previously reported agent configurations and adds BrowserUse with GPT-5.1 in Table 5, plus a human task-completion baseline in Sections 5.3 and 6. These substantially extend the comparison beyond agent-only performance. Sonnet-4.5 is mentioned in Section 5.2 but has no corresponding reported result row.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a 470-task public validation/400-task private test split with rotating private evaluation subsets. Evaluator validation changes from 50 to 400 task-trajectory pairs, and stability testing changes from 100 GPT-4o tasks to 800 BrowserUse tasks. The new human study specifies six participants, randomized task subsets, familiarization, and a 30-minute task limit.

E4.justification: v1 provides qualitative failure examples; v2 adds an extensive manually annotated failure-frequency analysis in Appendix 8.8 and Table 9, with detailed examination of seven categories. Table 6 also replaces the duplicated grounding example under Failed Repetition with an actual repetition case. Evaluator robustness validation is substantially expanded.

E5.justification: v1 reports ten judge runs and a single cross-run standard deviation. v2 reports five runs, adds perfect status/score agreement and per-task variability categories in Table 4, and specifies variability of per-run average scores. It also introduces human performance uncertainty of +/-3%, without defining that uncertainty's statistical meaning.

E6.justification: v2 adds BrowserUse GPT-5.1 results, including 22.2% overall success, human success of 90%, and failure-category counts. Evaluator agreement is reported as 93% on the revised 400-pair validation, versus 88% on 50 pairs in v1; these are different settings. All nine original agent result rows and the relocated domain/attribute scores retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The compositional task definition, scoring rubric, and formal mappings in v1 Appendix 9.4 and v2 Appendix 8.5, including equations (1)–(5), are substantively unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 makes quantifying the human-agent performance gap a central contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It also replaces the fully containerized benchmark framing with complementary live and Dockerized tracks and claims the most comprehensive Dockerized benchmark. The original end-to-end web data-science benchmark claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets human performance as evidence of task solvability and adds detailed explanations involving intent tracking, effort allocation, and long- versus short-horizon control. It acknowledges live-site instability and limits reproducibility to frozen environments. Conversely, v1's specific limitations concerning specialized-domain coverage, QA emphasis, privacy, and infrastructure risks are removed rather than relocated.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation disclosure: JSON task initialization, AgentBrain outputs, disabled procedural memory, DataFrame conversion, pickle caching, parallel workers, retries, and trajectory logging. It adds task-authoring/review details, a benchmark-access link, and submission instructions. Hardware reporting is corrected from 258 GB to 256 GB; these disclosures do not establish changed underlying implementations.

R1.justification: Related work adds DSBench, DA-Code, Spider 2.0, Spider2-V, and DABStep, and supplies an AgentOccam citation; the tool-failure reference by Treviño et al. is removed. The broad positioning against browsing-only and static data-analysis benchmarks remains, with an added claim about Dockerized benchmark comprehensiveness.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten, task formulation is moved before task generation, and benchmark-design and implementation explanations are expanded. A substantial task-example catalog is added, analysis subsections are reorganized, and the standalone limitations section disappears. These changes substantially reshape the document's exposition.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 1's music example with an enrollment-analysis workflow, adds stability and failure-frequency tables, and moves the domain/attribute results from main-text Table 5 to appendix Table 8. The conference template changes typography and page layout throughout. Figures 2–6 retain identical underlying images despite resizing or relocation.

improvement.justification: The human study, broader evaluator checks, quantified failure analysis, and implementation documentation improve support and transparency beyond v1. However, v2 still claims roughly 13% best-agent performance despite Table 5 reporting 22.2%; Table 9 counts sum to 768 rather than the stated 764. Unspecified human task counts and uncertainty definitions, together with removed limitations, constrain the value of the additions. The net improvement is limited.
